image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of the dorsal side of a large whale swimming in green water. The skin is dark grey/black with significant white mottling and patches, characteristic of barnacles or cyamids. A distinct longitudinal ridge runs along the spine. The head is not fully visible, but the rostrum area shows the typical arched shape. No dorsal fin is present, consistent with a grey whale. A small portion of a yellow object (likely a kayak or boat) is visible in the bottom left corner.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is partially cropped at the left edge; the blowholes are not visible in this frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey/black coloration with irregular white patches/scars consistent with barnacle/cyamid infestation.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is no dorsal fin. Instead, a series of low humps (knuckles) is visible along the midline of the back, which is a definitive trait of the grey whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible section of the body is thick and robust, consistent with the massive scale of a baleen whale.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed across the entire visible dorsal surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the whale is not visible; baleen plates are internal/ventral structures and cannot be seen in this dorsal view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pectoral fins are located on the ventral/lateral sides and are submerged or out of frame in this top-down shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin surface appears uneven and textured, not smooth like a dolphin or killer whale, consistent with callosities and barnacle bases.
